status: Complete source/test review; existing general structural-discovery mechanisms mapped.
insights: Database token filtering is already generic: holes and applied higher-order holes stop structural constraints, and only one subject site may satisfy a template; unrelated sites must not jointly satisfy it.
The in-memory matcher indexes concrete sorts and literal leaves in addition to heads; generic type variables omit sort constraints. Composite constructors are not literal leaves.
Small head buckets use direct matching; large buckets lazily construct inverted token postings and intersect rarest constraints first. This is a search scheduling decision, not proof authority.
Subject nodes, tokens and full inference attempts have distinct budgets. Unrelated heads do not spend inference attempts; repeated matches share the budget within one TemplateSites instance.

SQLite candidates run under an explicit read transaction and bounded token materialization, then return a complete union; its API deliberately has no page-limit parameter. Do not mechanically impose the pattern-reader page contract on this different API.
Missing/legacy indexes and unavailable pinned snapshot metadata fall back to paged canonical discovery. Full higher-order inference and kernel admission remain mandatory.

Tests compare accelerated discovery with exhaustive infer results, test irrelevant-head budget behavior,512literal alternatives,composite constructors,sorts and applied-hole binder order. They do not prove every legal template or corrupted-index behavior.
next: Prefer extending these existing generic mechanisms for new checked law families instead of building ad hoc per-rule indexes. Measure demand/selectivity before adding more token depth or caching. No new defect reproduced in these three files; broader higher-pattern/infer audit still required.
